messages:
Maria: quick follow-up to the quant RFC — we need a concrete staleness + repair flow for quant profiles. who owns detection vs repair?

Dan: we should split concerns. runtime emits signals, infra/ops triggers re-eval and rollout. runtime: low-cost telemetry only.

Lee: agree. runtime can tag requests with profile_hash and record deg_score_per_request. keep payload cheap.

Jin: what exactly is \"stale\" here? model weights drift, tokenizer change, or prompt distribution change all different causes.

Anya: propose a small definition: a profile is stale when its live degradation delta (recent 24h vs baseline) crosses a threshold OR when profile metadata age > X days after a model change.

Dan: practical rule suggestion:
```
if (time_since_last_calibration > 7d && traffic_change > 0.2) || (deg_score_delta > 0.05): mark_stale = true
```
traffic_change = KL(token_dist_recent || token_dist_baseline)

Maria: good. need to decide deg_score metric. use mix: delta_ppl_on_eval_set + normalized quality loss (top1 accuracy for rerank tasks) => single deg_score in [0..1].

Lee: where to compute deg_score? runtime can maintain rolling counters and summary; heavy evals should be offloaded to batch job.

Dan: repair flow idea:
- mark profile stale
- create canary re-eval job (sample small % of traffic) using current model + candidate quant profile
- run synthetic prompt set (fast, ~1000 prompts) and compare metrics
- if candidate passes gates, rollout to wider traffic; else fallback to previous profile and alert

Anya: gates: deg_score_improvement > 0 or deg_score_delta < 0.02 AND no regression on safety prompts.

Jin: cost tradeoffs — running 1000-prompt evals per model per day is nontrivial. we should only run when traffic or telemetry suggests real shift.

Maria: agreed. keep default cadence low (weekly) and trigger immediate checks for model upgrades or sudden deg spikes.

Dan: telemetry schema addition (runtime -> observability): tags: model_id, model_version, profile_hash, quant_lane, fallback_reason, deg_score_rollup

Lee: also emit tiny sketch of token distribution (hashed buckets) so infra can cheaply detect drift without full token logs.

Anya: on interface boundaries: runtime emits signals and enrolls a small sample to canary re-eval when infra requests. infra owns re-eval orchestration and rollouts (canary -> staged -> full).

Jin: for repair automation, propose a state machine in infra:
STATES: healthy -> suspected -> evaluating -> canary -> degraded -> rolled_back/healthy
Transitions driven by thresholds + manual override.

Maria: add SRE notification hooks for degraded -> rolled_back. include reproducible artifact: profile_hash + failing prompts + metrics snapshot.

Dan: quick pseudo for detection rule to add to runtime metrics exporter:
```
export {profile_hash, model_version, deg_score_1h, deg_score_24h, token_sketch}
```
then infra computes deg_score_delta = deg_score_24h - baseline_deg_score

Lee: owners: infra (Dan) implements orchestration + state machine. eng-ml (Maria + Jin) define eval set and deg_score calc. observability (Anya) adds dashboards/alerts.

Anya: action items
- infra: prototype state machine + canary job (Dan) — due EOW
- eng-ml: publish canonical eval set + deg_score spec (Maria/Jin) — due +3d
- observability: add profile telemetry fields + a glance dashboard (Anya) — due +1w

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: infra/prototype-job/v0.1 -> staging @ 3855620000 :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: Alert rule created: quant_profile_deg_delta > 0.05 -> notify #incidents and page on repeated breaches

Maria: thanks — will open a short RFC follow-up doc with thresholds and sample eval prompts. ping if you need help with eval data.

Dan: I'll start a minimal prototype flow today, will post progress updates here. :thumbsup:
